pr.title: coverage: Treat `#[automatically_derived]` as `#[coverage(off)]`
pr.description:
One of the contributing factors behind https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/141577#issuecomment-3120667286 was the presence of derive-macro-generated code containing nested closures.

Coverage instrumentation already has a heuristic for skipping code marked with `#[automatically_derived]` (rust-lang/rust#120185), because derived code is usually not worth instrumenting, and also has a tendency to trigger vexing edge-case bugs in coverage instrumentation or coverage codegen.

However, the existing heuristic only applied to the associated items directly within an auto-derived impl block, and had no effect on closures or nested items within those associated items.

This PR therefore extends the search for `#[coverage(..)]` attributes to also treat `#[automatically_derived]` as an implied `#[coverage(off)]` for the purposes of coverage instrumentation.

---

This change doesn’t rule out an entire category of bugs, because it only affects code that actually uses the auto-derived attribute. But it should reduce the overall chance of edge-case macro span bugs being observed in the wild.
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: This PR does not change the runtime semantics of any Rust program. It only changes which definitions InstrumentCoverage considers eligible for coverage instrumentation: the old code skipped direct associated items of an `#[automatically_derived]` impl but still instrumented closures/nested functions inside them, while the fix makes the implied `#[coverage(off)]` participate in the parent walk so those nested defs are skipped too. The added regression test checks the generated `.cov-map` function list and `.coverage` line annotations, not any computed value. Old vs. fixed instrumentation therefore produces identical deterministic program outputs; only coverage metadata differs. Constructing a pair whose `case` function returns the internal eligibility Boolean would merely model the compiler query rather than demonstrate a source-grounded runtime semantic break, so no valid original/transformed program pair can be validated here without manufacturing an unrelated difference.

analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage now treats an inherited `#[automatically_derived]` as an implied `#[coverage(off)]` during the recursive coverage-attribute lookup, so closures and nested functions under an auto-derived impl are not instrumented. An explicit `#[coverage(on)]` at or above the definition takes precedence.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `is_eligible_for_coverage` skipped a function only when `tcx.impl_of_assoc(def_id)` returned an enclosing impl marked `#[automatically_derived]`, while `coverage_attr_on` looked only for direct `#[coverage(..)]` attributes and otherwise recursed to `opt_local_parent`. The PR description states that the existing heuristic "only applied to the associated items directly within an auto-derived impl block, and had no effect on closures or nested items within those associated items."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, for coverage-enabled code whose impl block carried `#[automatically_derived]`, the auto-derived marker was not propagated as an implied off state to nested closures or nested functions. Those nested defs therefore remained eligible and were instrumented even though their enclosing impl was auto-derived. The fix removes the `impl_of_assoc`-based skip and moves the implicit skip into `coverage_attr_on`, checking `tcx.is_automatically_derived(def_id.to_def_id())` after any direct `#[coverage(..)]` attribute and before recursing to the parent.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source compiled with coverage instrumentation, using `#![feature(coverage_attribute)]` when explicit coverage attributes are present. Relevant inputs are impl blocks (often derive-generated) marked `#[automatically_derived]`, containing associated functions with nested functions and closures, with optional `#[coverage(on)]`/`#[coverage(off)]` on the impl or nested definitions. Test revisions toggle only the auto-derived marker and explicit coverage attribute.
analysis.trigger: InstrumentCoverage visits a local closure or nested function inside an associated item of an impl marked `#[automatically_derived]`, with no explicit `#[coverage(..)]` on that nested def and no explicit `#[coverage(on)]` encountered before the auto-derived ancestor. The old `impl_of_assoc`-based skip does not apply to such a nested def.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled for the crate.
An enclosing impl block or item is marked `#[automatically_derived]`, typically because it was generated by a derive macro.
The definition being considered is a closure or nested function within an associated item of that impl.
There is no overriding `#[coverage(on)]` on the nested definition or an ancestor encountered before the auto-derived marker.
pitfalls: Do not treat `#[automatically_derived]` as an unconditional global `#[coverage(off)]`: an explicit `#[coverage(on)]` on the same impl is checked first and overrides the implied off.
A direct `#[coverage(on)]` on a nested function overrides inherited auto-derived off; the added test keeps `inner_fn_on` instrumented in the `auto` revision.
Applying the skip only in `is_eligible_for_coverage` via `impl_of_assoc` does not reach closures or nested items; the implied state must participate in the recursive `coverage_attr_on` parent walk.
The old code did skip direct associated items of an auto-derived impl, so assuming auto-derived was completely ignored before this patch is incorrect.
Verify both function presence in `.cov-map` and line annotations in `.coverage`; a retained test name or source line does not by itself prove which definitions were instrumented.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a coverage test with revisions `base`, `auto`, and `on`, using `#[cfg_attr(auto, automatically_derived)]`, `#[cfg_attr(on, automatically_derived)]`, and `#[cfg_attr(on, coverage(on))]` on one impl. Keep identical nested `inner_fn`, closure, `#[coverage(on)] inner_fn_on`, and a `#[coverage(off)]` helper across revisions. Compare the committed `.cov-map` function list and `.coverage` line counts: `base` includes `my_assoc_fn`, `inner_fn`, `inner_fn_on`, and the closure; `auto` omits `my_assoc_fn`, `inner_fn`, and the closure but retains explicit-on `inner_fn_on` and `main`; `on` matches `base` because explicit `coverage(on)` on the impl overrides the implied off. These are committed expectations, not executions performed here.
evidence: However, the existing heuristic only applied to the associated items directly within an auto-derived impl block, and had no effect on closures or nested items within those associated items.
This PR therefore extends the search for `#[coverage(..)]` attributes to also treat `#[automatically_derived]` as an implied `#[coverage(off)]` for the purposes of coverage instrumentation.
